metadata.title: Stock Picking in Difficult Times with George Noble | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 76
metadata.transcript_type: publisher machine transcript with speaker markers

transcript_hash_basis: Normalized source metadata records the underlying full transcript hash. All normalized segments were read.
summary: A September 2 recorded conversation with George Noble, published September 21, connects AI funding risk, heavy debt issuance, Japanese capital flows and narrative-driven valuations. Eisman stresses borrower profitability and customer concentration; Noble supplies the strongest AI-collapse and Tesla/SpaceX short claims. The review preserves Eisman's explicit statement that Noble may be more bearish than he is.
assessment: Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts George Noble. SPEAKER_00 generally denotes Eisman and SPEAKER_01 Noble, but speaker markers contain obvious turn-boundary errors. Guest short targets remain guest claims; the host's closing summary is not a wholesale endorsement.
framework_points: Trace supplier revenue to end-user economics and financing sources.
Circular financing is a warning signal, not automatic default.
Account for macro factors and currency exposure in stock selection.
Separate long-run investment value from daily price moves and technology usefulness.
Distinguish receivables concentration from revenue concentration.
tools_and_charts: Debt-to-GDP versus yield chart is described but not reconstructed.
Tesla Q3 financial summary and operating/FCF distinctions.
FIMA repo mechanics compared with the guest's swap-line account.
transcript_cautions: All 1,201 normalized transcript segments were read in full.
Noble explicitly dates the recording September 2, 2026 at about 1938 seconds; publication is September 21.
Publisher speaker markers sometimes assign both sides of an exchange to one label. Attribution follows question-and-answer context; short confirmations are not separate predictions.
Eisman's 40-basis-point AI rate effect is explicitly an invented illustrative number.
Tesla PDF financial table was inspected via primary-source search extraction; PDF screenshot output was not usable, and no claim of a complete PDF read is made.
No verified short-entry records or total trading returns were available.
materiality_note: Major investment theses are distinguished from supporting factual premises. No overall accuracy percentage is appropriate.

evidence.title: Statement by Finance Minister Katayama
evidence.finding: Confirms coordinated yen purchases with the U.S. Treasury on July 31 and plans to use the Federal Reserve FIMA Repo Facility. It does not announce a new Treasury currency swap or a loan to buy JGBs.

evidence.title: FIMA Repo Facility FAQs
evidence.finding: FIMA is a Federal Reserve repo facility allowing eligible foreign monetary authorities to obtain temporary dollars against Treasury collateral, avoiding outright Treasury sales. It is distinct from a currency swap and does not itself require JGB purchases.
